sense: a gadget: a phone, tablet or the like

terms.comment: Classically any implement or tool, and as a collective, equipment (see tool). An electronic device is īnstrūmentum ēlectronicum; where the kind is clear, name it: tēlephōnum, computātrum.
Late (Lewis & Short), but the modern word for small appliances, as in māchinula phōtographica (see camera) and māchinula calculātōria (see calculator).
Classically a preparing, then the things prepared: equipment, apparatus (Cic.); for a single device, too wide.

phrases.latin: Ante cēnam omnia īnstrūmenta ēlectronica sēpōnite.
phrases.english: Put all your devices away before dinner.

sources: Lewis & Short: instrumentum · Lewis & Short: machinula · Lewis & Short: apparatus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 305.
